AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Periostin, a protein present in the alveolar bone and periodontal ligament, related to response to external forces. The aims of this study are; to detect the levels of periostin in peri-implant sulcular ﬂuid (PISF) and gingival crevicular ﬂuid (GCF), and to evaluate the relationship between periostin, ICTP (Pyridinoline cross-linked carboxyterminal telopeptide of type 1 collagen) and CTX (C-terminal crosslinked telopeptide of type 1 collagen) levels and clinical inﬂammatory symptoms and duration of functional loading.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: The study population was constituted of 9 women and 4 men with mean age 43.23±12.48. Twenty 'bone-level designed' dental implants (DI) placed in the molar or premolar sites, without any signs of peri-implant bone loss and with a restoration in function for at least 12 months and twenty contralateral natural teeth (NT) were included in the study as controls. Clinical parameters and restoration dates of the implants were recorded. PISF and GCF ICTP, CTX and periostin levels were evaluated using ELISA.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: ICTP, CTX and Periostin levels were similar between DI and NT groups. There were no statistically signiﬁcant differences between PISF and GCF values. When implants were grouped as healthy (GI = 0) and inﬂamed (GI≥0), ICTP levels and PISF volume were lower in healthy implants compared to the inﬂamed group. Both, periostin and CTX levels were negatively correlated with functioning time suggesting less bone remodeling around dental implants at later stages of functioning.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Findings of this study suggest collagen breakdown products may be used as markers to evaluate peri-implant metabolism.
